Let $\Sigma$ and $\mathcal B$ be nonempty finite sets of feature types and score bins. A randomized risk assignment consists of scores $v_b\in[0,1]$ for $b\in\mathcal B$ and a single matrix $X_{\sigma b}\ge0$ with $\sum_{b\in\mathcal B}X_{\sigma b}=1$ for each $\sigma$; conditional on feature type $\sigma$, the assignment chooses bin $b$ with probability $X_{\sigma b}$, independently of group and outcome. Thus, for a group-$t$ individual chosen according to its feature distribution, $\Pr_t(\Sigma=\sigma,Y=1,B=b)=a_{t\sigma}p_\sigma X_{\sigma b}$ and $\Pr_t(\Sigma=\sigma,Y=0,B=b)=a_{t\sigma}(1-p_\sigma)X_{\sigma b}$, and the assigned score is $S=v_B$. $$

For an iid sample from this law and discrepancy $d(p,q)=|p_1-q_1|$, the full calibration error is $0.2$. If the entire forecast simplex is treated as one bin, the empirical binned calibration estimate converges almost surely to zero.

finite_smoke.result: The merged conditional success probability is (0.1+0.9)/2=0.5, while the original laws differ.
finite_smoke.asserts: Give $X\in\{a,b,c\}$ and the binary label $Y\in\{1,2\}$ their full power-set sigma-algebras. Let $X$ be uniform on $\{a,b,c\}$ and let the conditional probabilities be $P(Y=1\mid X=a)=0.1$, $P(Y=1\mid X=b)=0.9$, and $P(Y=1\mid X=c)=0.75$. Coarsen the feature by $T(a)=T(b)=u$ and $T(c)=v$, and forecast $G=(P(Y=1\mid T),P(Y=2\mid T))$. Then $G(a)=G(b)=(0.5,0.5)$ and $G(c)=(0.75,0.25)$. This forecast is fully reliable, although it cannot distinguish $a$ from $b$, whose conditional label laws differ.
